onset.explanation: Reason: conflicting assessments (§6.4, A23). On 29 Jan a nurse scored ICE 9/10 at 20:15, which is Grade 1. A resident scored ICE 10/10 at 20:50, 35 minutes later, which is a formal Grade 0 assessment. If the 9/10 counts, onset is 2031-01-29: the record's 2031-01-30 is then 1 day late, which is category 7.1. If the 10/10 counts, the first qualifying finding is ICE 8/10 at 10:00 on 30 Jan, so onset is 2031-01-30, which matches the record (7.7). The two readings give different categories, so the result is 7.5. The 27 Jan ICE 10/10 is Grade 0, and the CRS fever is not a competing cause.

evidence.quote: Evening neurological check on 29 Jan at 20:15: ICE 9/10 (orientation 4/4, naming 3/3, commands 1/1, writing 1/1, attention 0/1).
On my examination at 20:50 on 29 Jan the ICE was 10/10 (all items complete including the counting task).
Morning check 30 Jan at 10:00: ICE 8/10 (orientation 3/4, attention 0/1, other items complete).

max_grade.explanation: The lowest ICE score is 8/10, on 30 Jan and again on 31 Jan, which is Grade 1. No note reaches a higher grade: the patient is awake throughout, and there is no seizure, focal motor deficit or edema finding. Headache is excluded from grading, and acetaminophen is not a competing cause. The conflicting reading on 29 Jan only changes the onset, not the grade. The documents support Grade 1, which equals the recorded Grade 1.

evidence.quote: ICE 8/10 (orientation 3/4, attention 0/1, other items complete). Awake.
ICE 8/10 at 09:30 on 31 Jan (orientation 3/4, attention 0/1). Awake, no focal deficit.
